sentences.text: On the basis of pleadings of parties following issues were framed by my Ld. Predecessor on 04.05.2023:

(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle no. DL-8CAM-0763 on 22.02.2022 at about 09:45 pm at main road near Himalaya Apartment, I.P.
Extension, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS Madhu Vihar in a rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Sh. Ashok Kumar?
OPP (2)Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so to what extent and from whom?
OPP (3)Relief.
7. On behalf of petitioner, two witnesses have been examined before Ld. LC.
PW1 is petitioner no.1 Sharda (wife of deceased) and PW2 is Jatin Kumar @ Sonu who is stated to be an eye witness.
No evidence has been led on behalf of respondent no. 1 and 2.
On behalf of respondent no.3 one witness namely Dr. S. Lal (HOD and Specialist, Department of Forensic Medicine, LBS Hospital) has been examined.
8. I have heard Sh. K.P. Singh, ld. counsel for petitioner and Mohd. Rafi, ld. counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company.
I have also gone through written arguments filed on behalf of petitioners.
Issue No.1 9.
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.

However, the standard of proof is not as MACT No.91/2022 SHELENDER SHELENDER Page 4 MALIK Date: 2024.10.04 16:15:54 +0530 strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

sentences.text: Therefore in view of this evidence come on record, this Tribunal is of the view that deceased died due to accidental injuries and in view of the evidence given by eye witness (PW2) and criminal case documents, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioners have established that vehicle no.DL-8CAM-0763 was in fact involved in the accident and decided died due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
Issue accordingly decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
Issue No.2 15.

In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to MACT No.91/2022 by SHELENDER Page 7 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.10.04 16:16:12 +0530 get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 16.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Ashok Kumar.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of MACT No.91/2022 SHELENDER by SHELENDER Page 9 MALIK MALIK
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.
The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased 18.
Petitioner no.1 Smt. Sharda (PW1) in her evidence has relied upon driving licence of deceased Ex.PW1/2 (colly.) as per which date of birth of the deceased is mentioned to be 12.04.1980.
There is no dispute with regard to this document as well as age of the deceased.
Thus, age of deceased as on the date of accident (22.02.2022) was 41 years 10 months.

Assessment of Income of deceased :
19.
Petitioner no.1 (PW1) in her deposition stated that her deceased husband was working as an auto driver at the time of accident and he was having monthly income of more than Rs.20,000/- per month.
However during cross examination PW1 admitted that she has not filed any proof of income and education of her deceased husband on record.
Witness also stated that during the period of accident her husband was not having any bank account.
No documentary evidence has been placed on record by the petitioners to prove the work and income of the deceased.

In the absence of any evidence and material either oral or documentary, this MACT No.91/2022 by SHELENDER Page 10 SHELENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.10.04 16:16:30 +0530 Tribunal is of the view that petitioners have failed to prove that deceased was working as an auto driver or that he used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month at the time of his death.

In the absence of any such material, income of deceased is taken to be at parity with minimum wages of skilled worker in the State of Delhi in view of the fact that driving licence of deceased has been proved on record, which at the time of accident was of Rs.19,473/- per month.
Application of Multiplier 20.
As held above, deceased was around 41 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.

This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

(iv) In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

23. Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 41 years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 25% of the income of deceased (aged between 40 to 50 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.

opennyai_summary.issue:
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving the offending vehicle no. DL-8CAM-0763 on 22.02.2022 at about 09:45 pm at main road near Himalaya Apartment, I.P.
Extension, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS Madhu Vihar in a rash and negligent manner and caused the death of deceased Sh. Ashok Kumar?
OPP (2)Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so to what extent and from whom?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as MACT No.91/2022 SHELENDER SHELENDER Page 4 MALIK Date: 2024.10.04 16:15:54 +0530 strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others (MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012), Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
10.
Therefore in view of this evidence come on record, this Tribunal is of the view that deceased died due to accidental injuries and in view of the evidence given by eye witness (PW2) and criminal case documents, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioners have established that vehicle no.DL-8CAM-0763 was in fact involved in the accident and decided died due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)
The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
23. Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 41 years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 25% of the income of deceased (aged between 40 to 50 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.
Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses:
24.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and MACT No.91/2022
